# Canon language reference

Canon v0.3, complete. Every sample here passes `canon check`.

## Text

Files end in .cn. Braces delimit blocks; indent two spaces; one statement per line. Comments are whole lines starting with #. Strings use double quotes. Types and variants are PascalCase; all other names are snake_case. A call's `(` must be on the function name's line.

## Types

Int (53-bit), Float (64-bit), Bool, String, Unit, `List[T]`, `Map[K, V]` (K is Int, Float or String), tuples `(A, B)`, functions `fn(A) -> B`. Built in: `Option[T]` is `Some(value: T) | None`; `Result[T, E]` is `Ok(value: T) | Err(error: E)`; `Error { message: String }`. Generic: `type Box[T] { value: T, }`.

```canon name=types
type Item {
  sku: String,
  qty: Int,
  price: Float,
}

type Step =
  | Call(tool: String)
  | Answer(text: String)
```

## Functions and effects

Parameter and return types are always written; locals never are. Optional clauses, one per line, in order: `effects:` (exactly those used, from fs, io, net, rand, time; none means pure), `requires:`, `ensures:` (`result` is the return value). Contracts must be pure (E103). Generic: `fn id[T](x: T) -> T`. Calling, naming (`map(xs, print)`) or using in a lambda an effectful function uses its effect.

A program performs only the effects its entry point declares (checked, and enforced at run time). Function types carry no effects: `fn apply(f: fn(String) -> Unit, s: String)` is pure yet prints when passed `print`; the caller naming `print` declares io.

## Statements

`let x = e` (immutable); `var x = e` (mutable); `x = e` or `x.field = e` on a var (field assignment rebinds x to an updated copy); `return e` (always explicit); `if c { } else if c { } else { }`; `for x in xs { }` (Lists only); `for (i, x) in enumerate(xs) { }` (names each tuple slot; `_` skips one); `while c { }`; `break` alone on its line leaves the innermost loop (no continue); a call, or `try` of a call, on its own line.

Tests: `test "name" { assert(...) }`. io, time and rand are free in tests (virtual clock and seed); a test using fs or net declares it with `effects: fs` on the line after its name.

```canon include=types
fn restock(items: List[Item], n: Int) -> Float
  effects: io
  requires: n >= 0
  ensures: result >= 0.0
{
  var total = 0.0
  for i in items {
    if i.qty < n {
      print(i.sku)
      total = total + to_float(n - i.qty) * i.price
    }
  }
  return total
}

fn first_short(words: List[String]) -> Int {
  var at = -1
  for (i, w) in enumerate(words) {
    if str_len(w) < 3 && w != "" {
      at = i
      break
    }
  }
  return at
}

test "first short" {
  assert(first_short(["canon", "", "is"]) == 2)
}
```

## Expressions

Precedence, loosest first: `|>` and lambdas; `||`; `&&`; `== != < <= > >=` (never chained); `+ -`; `* / %`; unary `-`, `!` and `try`; calls `f(x)`, fields `a.b`, tuple slots `t.0`. So `!(a == b)` needs its parentheses.

No methods, no indexing. Literals: `[1, 2]`, `(a, b)`, `P { x: 1, y: 2 }`; no unit literal. Lambda bodies are one expression: `|a, b| a + b`; an n-parameter lambda given one n-tuple unpacks it. `match e { pattern => expr, }` is an expression allowed anywhere: one arm per line, first match wins, exhaustive. Patterns: `_`, a name, a literal, a variant `Some(x)`, a tuple `(a, b)`, nested.

Arithmetic takes two Ints or two Floats; mixing is T009 (use `to_float`). Int division truncates toward zero. `+` also joins two Strings; String with Int is T001 (use `to_string`). `<` etc. take Int, Float or String; `==` is structural on any one type except functions. `&&` and `||` short-circuit. Values are immutable; lambdas capture values.

`x |> f(y)` means `f(x, y)`. Three or more chained calls must be a pipeline, one stage per line; fewer must be nested calls. A call whose first argument is a literal, like `range(0, n)`, can head a pipeline but is never a stage.

`try e` on a Result gives v for `Ok(v)` and returns `Err(x)` early for `Err(x)`; the enclosing function must return a Result with that error type. No `try` in lambdas or tests. A hole `?` or `?name` marks an unknown expression; H001 reports its type and candidate functions.

```canon include=types
fn label(item: Item) -> String {
  return item.sku + (match item.qty {
    0 => " out",
    _ => " in",
  })
}

fn cheapest(items: List[Item]) -> List[String] {
  return items
    |> filter(|i| i.qty > 0 && i.price > 0.0)
    |> sort_by(|i| i.price)
    |> map(|i| i.sku)
}
```

## Canonical form and the fix loop

`check` rejects any file `fmt` would change (C001, with the patch). fmt fixes spacing, parentheses, commas, `else { if }`, `== true`/`== false`, `!!`, numbers, `use`, effect and clause order, pipeline versus nesting, and old spellings (`and`/`or`/`not`, `set`); it breaks a statement over 100 characters at its outermost list, tuple, record or call brackets, one item per line with trailing commas.

Run `canon check --fix --write --json FILE`. It applies every C001, E101, E102 and T009 patch until none is left and returns only what needs you. T001 may list candidate patches in `data.suggestions` (`to_string(e)`, `unwrap_or(e, ?)`, `Some(e)`, ...): apply the one you mean. T004's patch adds missing arms as holes; apply it, then fill them. Repeat until `"ok": true`.

## Running and CLI

`canon run` calls `fn main() -> Unit` (or a main returning a Result; Err prints and exits 1). requires is checked on entry, ensures on every return. `canon test` runs test blocks, then calls each pure, non-generic function with a contract on 200 seeded generated inputs; a failure prints `FAIL fuzz name: a = -19, b = 12` and the trap.

Commands: `canon check [--fix [--write]]`, `fmt [--write]`, `run [--deny fs,net] [--no-contracts]`, `test`; each takes files and `--json`. Exit 0 ok, 1 on diagnostics, failed tests or traps, 2 usage error.

## Standard library

No overloading. Letters are type parameters; K is Int, Float or String; xs is a `List[A]`, m a `Map[K, V]`. Pure unless an effect is shown.

```text
len(xs) -> Int; reverse(xs) -> List[A]; enumerate(xs) -> List[(Int, A)]
map(xs, fn(A) -> B) -> List[B]; filter(xs, fn(A) -> Bool) -> List[A]
fold(xs, init: B, fn(B, A) -> B) -> B
sum(List[Int]) -> Int; sum_float(List[Float]) -> Float
sort_by, sort_desc_by(xs, key: fn(A) -> K) -> List[A]   stable
group_by(xs, key: fn(A) -> K) -> List[(K, List[A])]   first-seen order
take, drop(xs, n: Int) -> List[A]; first, last(xs) -> Option[A]
append(xs, A) -> List[A]; contains(xs, A) -> Bool; zip(xs, List[B]) -> List[(A, B)]
range(start: Int, end: Int) -> List[Int]   end excluded
min, max(Int, Int) -> Int; abs(Int) -> Int; pow(base: Int, exp: Int) -> Int
to_float(Int) -> Float; to_int(Float) -> Int (truncates); to_string(T) -> String
parse_int(String) -> Option[Int]; parse_float(String) -> Option[Float]
join(List[String], sep: String) -> String; split(String, sep: String) -> List[String]
trim(String) -> String; str_len(String) -> Int
unwrap_or(Option[T], fallback: T) -> T; assert(Bool) -> Unit, traps R005
map_from(List[(K, V)]) -> m; map_get(m, K) -> Option[V]; map_set(m, K, V) -> m
keys(m) -> List[K]; values(m) -> List[V]   insertion order
io: print(String) -> Unit; read_line() -> Option[String]
fs: read_file(path: String) -> Result[String, Error]
  write_file(path: String, text: String) -> Result[Unit, Error]
net: http_get(url: String) -> Result[String, Error]
  http_post(url: String, body: String) -> Result[String, Error]
time: now() -> Int (ms since epoch); sleep(ms: Int) -> Unit
rand: random() -> Float in [0, 1); random_int(lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int, hi excluded
```

## Diagnostics

`canon check --json` prints `{ ok, canonical, diagnostics }`; each has code, message, line, col, maybe `data` and `fix.diff` (a unified diff to apply as is). `--fix` adds `applied` and `source`.

P001 parse · P002 comment placement · P003 local annotation · P004 non-call statement · P005 stage not a call · C001 not canonical · L001 line over 100 chars fmt cannot break (bind with let) · N001 naming · M001 `use` other than `std.<name>` · E100 unknown effect · E101 undeclared effect · E102 unused effect · E103 effect in a contract · H001 hole · T001 type mismatch · T002 unknown name · T003 argument count · T004 non-exhaustive match · T005 missing return · T006 assigning a non-var · T007 misplaced try · T008 unknown field · T009 Int and Float mixed · T010 break outside a loop.

Traps print one JSON object (code, message, line, col, stack): R001 requires failed · R002 ensures failed · R003 Int overflow · R004 division by zero · R005 assert failed · R006 effect denied by the host

# Canon language reference (Canon-Py)

Canon v0.4 in its Canon-Py syntax, complete. Canon-Py is typed Python syntax with Canon's rules: same checker, same guarantees, a strict subset of the forms. Check, run and format with `--syntax py`. Every sample here passes `canon check --syntax py`.

## Text

Files end in .cn. Indent 4 spaces; one statement per line; one blank line between top-level definitions. Comments are whole lines starting with #. Strings use double quotes. Types and variants are PascalCase; all other names are snake_case.

## Types

int (53-bit), float (64-bit), bool, str, None (no value), `list[T]`, `dict[K, V]` (K is int, float or str), `tuple[A, B]`, functions `Callable[[A], B]`. Built in: `Option[T]` is `Some(value: T) | None`; `Result[T, E]` is `Ok(value: T) | Err(error: E)`; `class Error` with `message: str`. Generic: `class Box[T]:`.

```canon syntax=py name=types
class Item:
    sku: str
    qty: int
    price: float

type Step = Call(tool: str) | Answer(text: str)
```

A record is a `class` with typed fields only (no methods, no inheritance), built with keywords: `Item(sku="a", qty=1, price=2.5)`. A sum type is one `type` line; variants are built by position: `Call("search")`.

## Functions and effects

Every `def` has parameter and return types; locals never do. Decorators, in order: `@effects(...)` (exactly those used, from fs, io, net, rand, time; none means pure), `@requires(cond)`, `@ensures(cond)` (`result` is the return value). Contracts must be pure (E103). Generic: `def first[T](xs: list[T]) -> Option[T]:`. Calling, naming (`each(xs, print)`) or using in a lambda an effectful function uses its effect.

Function types carry effects: `Callable[[str], None, io]` performs io when called, `Callable[[str], None]` is pure. Calling a function value performs its type's effects; passing an effectful function where a pure function type is expected is T011. So every signature bounds what its function can do, and a program performs only the effects its entry point declares (checked, and enforced at run time).

## Statements

`x = e` binds x the first time and assigns it after (mutability is inferred); `x += e` (also `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`); `p.field = e` rebinds p to an updated copy. Names live in the block that binds them: bind before an `if` to use after it. Assigning a parameter rebinds a local copy; callers never see it (values are immutable). `return e` (always explicit); `if c:` / `elif c:` / `else:`; `for x in xs:` (lists only); `for i, x in enumerate(xs):`; `while c:`; `break` (no continue); `pass` for an empty block; `assert cond`; a call, or `e?` of a call, on its own line.

`match e:` with `case pattern:` lines; each case body is exactly one statement, and all cases end the same way: all `return e`, all `name = e` to the same name, or all calls. First match wins; it must be exhaustive. Patterns: `_`, a name, a literal, a variant `Some(x)` or `None`, a tuple `(a, b)`, nested.

Tests: `def test_name() -> None:` with asserts. io, time and rand are free in tests (virtual clock and seed); a test using fs or net declares `@effects(fs)`.

```canon syntax=py include=types
@effects(io)
@requires(n >= 0)
@ensures(result >= 0.0)
def restock(items: list[Item], n: int) -> float:
    total = 0.0
    for i in items:
        if i.qty < n:
            print(i.sku)
            total += to_float(n - i.qty) * i.price
    return total

def first_short(words: list[str]) -> int:
    at = -1
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if str_len(w) < 3 and w != "":
            at = i
            break
    return at

def describe(s: Step) -> str:
    match s:
        case Call(tool):
            return f"call {tool}"
        case Answer(text):
            return text

def test_first_short() -> None:
    assert first_short(["canon", "", "is"]) == 2
```

## Expressions

Precedence, loosest first: `lambda`; `a if c else b`; `or`; `and`; `not`; `== != < <= > >= in not in is is not` (never chained); `+ -`; `* / %`; unary `-`; calls `f(x)`, fields `a.b`, tuple slots `t[0]`, `e?`.

No methods, and no indexing except tuple slots `t[0]`. Literals: `[1, 2]`, `(a, b)`, `True`, `False`. No comprehensions, dict literals or keyword arguments (except to build records). `x in xs` tests a list; `x is None` tests an Option. f-strings: `f"{n} items"` (no format specs). Lambdas are one expression: `lambda a, b: a + b`; an n-parameter lambda given one n-tuple unpacks it. `a if c else b` chooses on a bool.

Arithmetic takes two ints or two floats; mixing is T009 (use `to_float`). **`/` on ints truncates toward zero, and `%` takes the dividend's sign; there is no `//` or `**` (use `pow`).** `+` joins two strs; str with int is T001 (use an f-string). `<` etc. take int, float or str; `==` is structural on any one type except functions. `and` and `or` short-circuit.

`e?` on a Result gives v for `Ok(v)` and returns `Err(x)` early for `Err(x)`; the enclosing function must return a Result with that error type. No `?` in lambdas or tests. A hole `...` marks an unknown expression; H001 reports its type and candidate functions.

```canon syntax=py include=types
def parse_qty(s: str) -> Result[int, str]:
    match parse_int(s):
        case Some(n):
            return Ok(n)
        case None:
            return Err(f"not a number: {s}")

def total_qty(a: str, b: str) -> Result[int, str]:
    x = parse_qty(a)?
    y = parse_qty(b)?
    return Ok(x + y)

def cheapest(items: list[Item]) -> list[str]:
    in_stock = filter(items, lambda i: i.qty > 0 and i.price > 0.0)
    return map(sort_by(in_stock, lambda i: i.price), lambda i: i.sku)
```

## Canonical form and the fix loop

`check` rejects any file `fmt` would change (C001, with the patch). fmt fixes spacing, indentation, blank lines, parentheses, commas, quotes, `else: if` to `elif`, `x = x + e` to `x += e`, `"a" + to_string(n)` to an f-string, `contains(xs, x)` to `x in xs`, `== None` to `is None`, `== True`, and effect and decorator order; it breaks a statement over 100 characters at its brackets, one item per line with trailing commas.

Run `canon check --syntax py --fix --write --json FILE`. It applies every C001, E101, E102 and T009 patch until none is left and returns only what needs you. T001 may list candidate patches in `data.suggestions` (`to_string(e)`, `unwrap_or(e, ...)`, `Some(e)`, ...): apply the one you mean. T004's patch adds missing cases as holes; apply it, then fill them. Repeat until `"ok": true`.

## Running and CLI

`canon run` calls `def main() -> None:` (or a main returning a Result; Err prints and exits 1). requires is checked on entry, ensures on every return. `canon test` runs the test functions, then calls each pure, non-generic function with a contract on 200 seeded generated inputs; a failure prints `FAIL fuzz name: a = -19, b = 12` and the trap.

Commands, each with `--syntax py`: `canon check [--fix [--write]]`, `fmt [--write]`, `run [--deny fs,net] [--no-contracts]`, `test`, `build [-o OUT] [--module]`; each takes files and `--json`; `--watch` reruns on save. Exit 0 ok, 1 on diagnostics, failed tests or traps, 2 usage error.

## Standard library

No overloading. Letters are type parameters; K is int, float or str; xs is a `list[A]`, m a `dict[K, V]`. Pure unless an effect is shown. Function arguments must be pure.

```text
len(xs) -> int; reverse(xs) -> list[A]; enumerate(xs) -> list[tuple[int, A]]
map(xs, Callable[[A], B]) -> list[B]; filter(xs, Callable[[A], bool]) -> list[A]
fold(xs, init: B, Callable[[B, A], B]) -> B
sum(list[int]) -> int; sum_float(list[float]) -> float
sort_by, sort_desc_by(xs, key: Callable[[A], K]) -> list[A]   stable
group_by(xs, key: Callable[[A], K]) -> list[tuple[K, list[A]]]   first-seen order
take, drop(xs, n: int) -> list[A]; first, last(xs) -> Option[A]
append(xs, A) -> list[A]; contains(xs, A) -> bool; zip(xs, list[B]) -> list[tuple[A, B]]
range(start: int, end: int) -> list[int]   end excluded
min, max(int, int) -> int; abs(int) -> int; pow(base: int, exp: int) -> int
to_float(int) -> float; to_int(float) -> int (truncates); to_string(T) -> str
parse_int(str) -> Option[int]; parse_float(str) -> Option[float]
join(list[str], sep: str) -> str; split(str, sep: str) -> list[str]

unwrap_or(Option[T], fallback: T) -> T; assert(bool), traps R005
map_from(list[tuple[K, V]]) -> m; map_get(m, K) -> Option[V]; map_set(m, K, V) -> m
keys(m) -> list[K]; values(m) -> list[V]   insertion order
io: print(str) -> None; read_line() -> Option[str]
fs: read_file(path: str) -> Result[str, Error]

net: http_get(url: str) -> Result[str, Error]

time: now() -> int (ms since epoch); sleep(ms: int) -> None
rand: random() -> float in [0, 1); random_int(lo: int, hi: int) -> int, hi excluded
```

## Diagnostics

`canon check --json` prints `{ ok, canonical, diagnostics }`; each has code, message, line, col, maybe `data` and `fix.diff` (a unified diff to apply as is). `--fix` adds `applied` and `source`.

    while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
